summary: Round r1 (restricted network). International scenario integration for S01-S10: each of the 28 existing scenario shocks is mapped to its channel, variable, unit and timing, the external variables (X01-X41 from 16A), the supplying and supporting Division B subagents, domestic counterparts and the source leads that would quantify it; all magnitudes remain null and every empirical item is PENDING. Seven declared scenario channels have no shock. Running the engine's compose() on S10 shows shared-key and different-timing overlaps: the S01/S04 remittance shocks share a key and S04-a is dropped as a 'duplicate' only because both are null, while tourism and real-growth shocks with different timing would add. Fifteen overlap checks (incl. X15 split between 24A/24C, remittance shocks across S01/S04/S06/S10, fuel price vs supply, electricity export capacity, preference-loss attribution, baseline-vs-event overlap) are recorded with proposed rules. Eleven reported 2026 events (Middle East conflict, LDC extension request, Rasuwa/Kyirong flood, Gulf permit suspension, Indian import measures, oil shock and others) are held in an unverified-events register with verification leads; none is treated as fact. Ten scenario YAML edits are proposed for the human reviewer and have not been applied. No numbers were taken from search snippets or memory.

Fifteen overlap checks with proposed rules are in specific.overlap_checks; resolution is pending evidence and a reviewer decision on an S10 override rule.

assumptions.text: Scenario shock units follow engine SHOCK_UNITS (pct_change = proportional change in level, decimal; pp = decimal percentage-point change in a rate). These are scenario-schema codes, distinct from src/economic_model/units.py unit codes used in finding values; a documented mapping is proposed (challenge to 00C).

A compound scenario should apply each causal pathway once; where components share a model variable, the compound's joint magnitude is an evidence question, not the sum, max or first of component magnitudes.
External flow and price shocks are expressed in foreign-currency terms (USD or INR); NPR effects enter only via the exchange_rate channel.
Aggregate_real_growth shocks are residual effects not captured by the scenario's other quantified channels.
Reported events are neither facts nor scenario inputs until verified; scenarios remain hypothetical stress tests with no probabilities.

challenges.text: compose() treats two null magnitudes as identical ('duplicate_counted_once') and on differing magnitudes nulls the merged shock; run_scenario() sums different-key shocks on the same projection variable. Request: (a) do not classify null==null as duplicate - report 'shared_key_pending'; (b) allow a compound-level shock with the same key to override components; (c) flag same-variable/different-timing shocks (S01-e/S04-b, S04-d/S05-d) as overlaps. 16C does not edit engine code.

24A notes 'pct_change' is not a units.py code. Scenario shocks are validated against engine SHOCK_UNITS, not units.py; please document the mapping (pct_change -> decimal ratio change; pp -> percentage_points/100) in docs/methodology to avoid mis-scaling.

Accept 24A/24C split of X15 into X15a (demand) and X15b (substitution); accept 17A's proposed variable for Indian import-side measures; X10 split per 17B (operating status vs announced projects). Update global_task_list in r2 (16A is the owner).

Exposure-register notes for EXP-02, EXP-13 and EXP-20 should reference unverified events E04, E02 and E03 (status 'lead-corroborated, pending retrieval' where tier-1 leads exist), without values; EXP-13 carries the graduation date as a two-branch dated attribute.

Please supply a single joint remittance response for the S10 compound state in addition to S01 and S04 partial responses, and state whether each is on NRB formal or total-receipts basis (OV-01, OV-11).

Escalation: S10 composition currently drops S04's remittance shock and may double count tourism and real-growth shocks; any quantified S10 result would be affected. Also OV-13: base-year choice relative to the reported 2026 events changes how S01/S05/S08 shocks are defined.

Red-team request: review OV-01..OV-15 and the unverified-events register; in particular whether S10 should also include S06 (origin-side and destination-side migration restrictions co-occurring) and supplier-continuity assumptions for petroleum (22A challenge). 16C will not modify Agent 28 findings.

uncertainty: Structural uncertainty dominates: no shock is quantified, the base year is pending, and the engine composition rule for shared keys is unresolved. Overlap judgements are based on channel definitions and scenario YAML, and may change when BoP/sector/household modules define transmission explicitly. The unverified events register relies on leads only (news and not-yet-retrieved official pages); any of those events could be mis-dated, mis-scoped or conflated (e.g. the 2025 vs 2026 Rasuwa events). Fiscal-year (Nepal, mid-July) vs calendar-year (international) mismatches affect every mapping from evidence to scenario timing. No probabilities are assigned to any scenario or event.

overlap_checks.finding: Identical engine key. compose() on the current YAML reports kind 'duplicate_counted_once' only because both magnitudes are null (None == None); S04-a is then silently dropped from S10. Once quantified with different magnitudes the engine marks the merged shock 'conflicting_magnitudes' and sets it to null, so S10 would carry no remittance shock at all.
overlap_checks.double_count_risk: Summing a conflict-driven and a recession-driven remittance fall would double count the GCC-oil-price pathway common to both; taking either alone would under-state the compound case.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: S10 needs its own jointly calibrated remittance shock (23C with 19D/23A), stated as a single magnitude for the combined state, with the S01/S04 components listed as evidence; the component keys stay but S10's own shock should override them (requires engine rule: parent shock with the same key takes precedence). Until then S10 remittance status is PENDING.

overlap_checks.finding: Migrant stock (S01-b), new labour permits (S06-a) and remittances (S01-a, S06-b) are linked: channel migrant_employment lists remittances among its model variables. If a remittance shock is calibrated from total NRB inflows it already contains the stock/flow effect; transmitting S01-b or S06-a into remittances again double counts. S06-b (1,3) and S01-a (1,2) have different keys and would stack if S06 were ever combined with S01 (e.g. the 2026 permit suspension, event E04, is a migration restriction originating in Nepal, not in destinations).
overlap_checks.double_count_risk: high once the BoP/household module transmits migrant_employment to remittances
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Migrant stock/permit shocks feed only domestic_labour_supply and household composition; remittance shocks are the single entry for secondary income. Record in each shock note. Classify the 2026 origin-side suspension under S01 (conflict response), not S06 (destination restriction).

overlap_checks.finding: (i) Within S01, aviation_connectivity lists tourism_demand as a model variable, so a seat-capacity shock plus a direct arrivals shock double counts. (ii) S01-e (tourist_arrivals, 1,1) and S04-b (tourist_arrivals, 1,2) have different keys, so compose() keeps both and a future tourism module would add them in the first year.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Treat S01-d as a capacity ceiling on arrivals (min operator), not an additive loss; in S10 calibrate a single joint arrivals path (21E with 19C) and align S01-e/S04-b timing keys or add an S10 override.

overlap_checks.finding: aggregate_real_growth is the only projection-applied channel here. S04-d (1,2) and S05-d (1,1) have different keys; run_scenario() sums magnitudes by projection variable, so in S10 both would be added in the first shocked year. Separately, S04-d and S05-d overlap their own scenarios' channel shocks, which will double count once BoP/sector modules transmit those channels to GDP (sector growth enters GDP only through value added).
overlap_checks.double_count_risk: high once sector/BoP modules exist; additive-summation question in S10 now
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Define aggregate_real_growth shocks explicitly as the residual not captured by other quantified channels, and require that when any sectoral channel of the same scenario becomes APPLIED the aggregate shock is recomputed. For S10, whether flood and recession GDP effects add is itself an evidence question (compound-event literature), not an engine default.

overlap_checks.finding: S01-c (petroleum_import_price) and S02-c (fuel_supply) are different variables and complementary (19E and 22A ask for joint treatment), but in S10 a price spike and a quantity constraint cannot both be applied independently to the import bill: rationed quantity at higher price is not price effect plus quantity effect computed separately from baseline.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Import bill in S10 = shocked price x constrained quantity, computed once; days-of-cover (19E) sets the constraint. Also keep retail pass-through vs NOC loss (fiscal) split (22A challenge).

overlap_checks.finding: S02-a shocks total imports; petroleum is a major import line and is shocked again by S02-c. A future essential-import shock (food/fertiliser/medicines, X29) would be a third overlapping cut.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Redefine S02-a as non-petroleum (and, if added, non-essential) imports, or compute total imports as the sum of disjoint components.

overlap_checks.finding: Electricity exports are reduced by market-access loss (S02-d), by generation loss (S05-b) and by price/volume change (S09). S05 declares electricity_trade without a shock (correct if derived). In S10, S02-d and S05-b both reduce export volume; applied multiplicatively on the baseline each, they can exceed what the constrained system could export.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Compute exports once as min(exportable surplus after S05-b, approved/available transfer capacity after S02-d); keep trilateral (Bangladesh) sales as a separate segment (17C). Keep dry-season imports on the same lines as a separate flow (22B).

overlap_checks.finding: X15 is split between 24C (market demand for digitally delivered services) and 24A (AI substitution of Nepal-supplied tasks). 24C's design already includes an AI-exposure 'demand-trend adjustment' using the same World Bank analyses 24A cites (24A-L10 = 24C-L12, 24A-L08 = 24C-L13). Applying 24A substitution on top of an AI-adjusted 24C demand path double counts. S07-b employment derived from exposure indices while S07-a uses deployment studies would also be internally inconsistent (24A: indices, deployment and administrative studies answer different questions).
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Split X15 into X15a (demand excluding AI substitution; 24C) and X15b (substitution rate on Nepal's task mix; 24A), S07-a = f(X15a, X15b) computed once; S07-b derived from S07-a with a labour-intensity parameter (08A), not independently. Also resolve the IT/BPO receipts recorded as remittances issue (21E) so S07-a and remittance shocks do not share a flow.

overlap_checks.finding: Both shock fdi with different timing keys (1,3 vs 1,2). Not jointly in any current compound scenario, but X23 and X41 are shared and diaspora investment (X35) may sit inside the FDI series (23E: NRN investment not confirmed separately identified).
overlap_checks.double_count_risk: low now; relevant if a new compound scenario combines S03 and S04
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Any future compound must use a single joint FDI path; state whether NRN investment is inside the base series.

overlap_checks.finding: goods_exports (S08-a) and exports (S02-b) and the declared-but-unshocked external_demand_goods (S04) can all capture the same export decline. Non-graduation shocks (US NTPP expiry, US reciprocal tariffs, Indian safeguard/anti-dumping measures - events E05/E08) must not be attributed to S08 (21A, 26C).
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Attribute export changes by cause and market: LDC-conditioned preference loss (S08) vs partner-demand (S04) vs Indian import-side policy (new variable proposed by 17A; S02 or a new policy shock) vs transit (S02). One shock per cause-market pair.

overlap_checks.finding: financial_compliance lists remittance_channel_formality; a compliance shock that shifts transfers to informal channels lowers NRB-recorded remittances without lowering household receipts. If the S01/S04 remittance shocks are calibrated on NRB formal inflows during a period that already includes a formality shift, S10-a double counts.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Calibrate remittance shocks on total receipts where possible (NLSS/KNOMAD) and apply S10-a only to the formal/informal split and to payment costs; report both formal and total.

overlap_checks.finding: exchange_rate is declared in S01/S02 without a shock. If remittance, fuel-price or capital-goods shocks are expressed in NPR, they would embed an exchange-rate effect that a later exchange_rate shock would repeat.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: All external price/flow shocks in USD or INR terms; NPR effects only through the exchange_rate channel (CLAUDE rule 6).

overlap_checks.finding: Baseline vs scenario overlap: several flagged 2026 events (E01-E05) fall in FY2025/26 or FY2026/27. The base year is PENDING. If the baseline vintage includes periods affected by a real event, applying the corresponding hypothetical shock on top double counts it; if not, the event is a candidate historical analogue for calibration.
overlap_checks.double_count_risk: high if the base year is set to FY2025/26 or later without adjustment
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: When 00A fixes the base year, 16C tags each verified event as 'inside baseline' or 'outside baseline'; scenario shocks are then defined relative to a baseline that either includes the event (shock = additional deterioration) or excludes it (event = analogue). No event enters any scenario before verification.

overlap_checks.finding: The reported 2026 Rasuwa event damaged a northern border crossing and hydropower. Northern-route transit (X10) is mapped by 16A to S02/S03/S05 but no S05 shock covers transit; 17B asks that northern transit capacity be zero-by-default in the baseline, in which case a northern-crossing loss has no first-order trade effect in the model and must not be imputed to S02-a (India).
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: Keep northern-crossing disruption out of S02 (India) and treat it, if needed, as a separate transit shock in S05 with its own evidence.

overlap_checks.finding: S02 declares agricultural_output. If an S02 shock were added on agriculture_gva with timing (1,1) it would share S05-c's key and, once magnitudes differ, compose() would null both in S10.
overlap_checks.rule_proposed: S02 agricultural pathway should use a supply variable (fertiliser_supply or food_imports) rather than agriculture_gva (PE-03).
